newsitem.title: NORWAY: Braathens SAFE airline 9-mo cargo sales up 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: Braathens SAFE airline 9-mo cargo sales up 11 pct.

text.p: Norwegian air carrier Braathens SAFE on Friday said its cargo sales rose by 11 percent to 124 million crowns in the first nine months of 1996.
The airline's managing director Erik Braathen said the carrier had no plans to expand its cargo operations, which include its express freight product Jetpak.
"(Revenue from cargo) is all based on cargo that we sell in the lower part of the aircraft so it's a...part of the passenger operation," Braathen told Reuters in an interview.
"We primarily focus on small parcel, high-yield delivery."

Braathens SAFE posted a pre-tax profit of 129 million crowns in the first nine months of 1996, down from 251 million a year earlier. The company cited increased price competition and higher operating costs.
Turnover for its cargo operations totalled 155 million crowns in 1995, a 12 percent increase over 1994.
